analysis.investment_thesis: MethodHub shows explosive top-line growth (35→57→135 Cr, ~96% CAGR) with strong reported ROE of 42.7%, but the IT services business lacks the innovation moat I look for, and weak cash conversion (FCF 4 Cr vs PAT 11 Cr) plus low promoter holding (26.85%) raise serious quality concerns. Not a "common stock with uncommon profits" — more a fast-growing micro-cap IT shop without proven differentiation.
key_strengths: Revenue scaled 3.9x in two years (35→135 Cr); PAT scaled 11x
key_risks: Cash conversion poor — OCF 5 Cr vs net profit 11 Cr in FY25
Low promoter stake at 26.85% with rising borrowings (26→39 Cr)
Generic IT services with no disclosed R&D, IP, or product moat
red_flags: Equity jumped 11→57 Cr in FY25 (likely IPO/dilution) — growth is partly inorganic/funded
Reported earnings not backed by operating cash flow
Tiny 144 Cr market cap with thin institutional ownership (FII 3.23%, DII 3.52%)
analysis.detailed_analysis: From a scuttlebutt perspective, MethodHub fails several of my 15 points. There is no visible R&D investment (point 2-3), no evidence of a differentiated sales organization (point 4), and the sub-30% promoter holding suggests management may not have skin in the game for the long haul (points 7-9). The IT staffing/consulting space in India is fiercely competitive — TCS, Infosys, Persistent and hundreds of mid-tier shops compete on the same talent pool. Without proprietary platforms or sticky enterprise relationships, margin durability is unproven. Operating margins of ~12-13% are decent but not exceptional for a "growth" classification.
